intro.title: Configuration that holds, teams that hold it.
intro.kicker: Two halves of the same job. The technical work keeps a server stable; the management work keeps it stable after I have left.

groups.title: Server configuration
groups.summary: Getting the platform right before a single plugin goes in.

skills.name: Paper & Purpur tuning
skills.note: View distance, entity limits, chunk loading and the config flags that actually move tick time.

skills.name: Velocity & proxy networks
skills.note: Multi-server routing, forwarding modes, shared player data and safe restart cycles.

skills.name: World management
skills.note: Multiverse setups, pregeneration, border control and seasonal world resets.

skills.name: Performance profiling
skills.note: Spark and timings reports read properly — fixing the cause rather than the symptom.

groups.title: Plugin configuration
groups.summary: Making twenty plugins behave like one coherent system.

skills.name: LuckPerms architecture
skills.note: Inherited tracks, contexts and per-server overrides that survive a rank rework.

skills.name: Economy & shop balancing
skills.note: Income sources paired with sinks, modelled before launch rather than patched after.

skills.name: Custom items & mobs
skills.note: ItemsAdder, MythicMobs and ModelEngine configured as one content pipeline.

skills.name: Config debugging
skills.note: Tracing conflicts between plugins competing for the same events and handlers.

skills.name: Protection & logging
skills.note: WorldGuard regions, CoreProtect retention and rollback procedures that work under pressure.

groups.title: Discord engineering
groups.summary: Structure and automation for communities that outgrew a single channel.

skills.name: Server architecture
skills.note: Channel trees, category permissions and progressive unlocks tied to member journey.

skills.name: Role & permission design
skills.note: Hierarchies that stay readable past thirty roles and never grant more than intended.

skills.name: Bot configuration
skills.note: Verification, tickets, logging and auto-moderation wired to a documented rule set.

skills.name: Minecraft ↔ Discord links
skills.note: Webhook relays for chat, punishments and rank sync across both platforms.

groups.title: Staff & team management
groups.summary: Building teams that make good calls without an owner in the room.

skills.name: Hiring & rubrics
skills.note: Written application scoring so hiring is repeatable rather than a vibe check.

skills.name: Training & onboarding
skills.note: Two-week onboarding paths with shadowing, checkpoints and a real sign-off.

skills.name: Rotas & coverage
skills.note: Shift planning across timezones with handover notes that actually get read.

skills.name: Escalation & delegation
skills.note: Clear ladders so every decision type has a named owner and a fallback.

skills.name: Performance reviews
skills.note: Regular one-to-ones and honest feedback before a problem becomes a departure.

groups.title: Community operations
groups.summary: Policy and process that survive contact with a real argument.

skills.name: Rules & policy writing
skills.note: Rule sets specific enough to enforce consistently and defend publicly.

skills.name: Conflict resolution
skills.note: De-escalation, mediation and appeals handled without picking sides by default.

skills.name: Moderation systems
skills.note: Punishment ladders, appeal routes and audit trails for every action taken.

skills.name: Retention & engagement
skills.note: Events and progression loops that bring players back without paying them to log in.

groups.title: Hosting & infrastructure
groups.summary: The unglamorous layer that decides how bad a bad night gets.

skills.name: Panel & host setup
skills.note: Pterodactyl nodes, allocations, resource limits and sane restart schedules.

skills.name: Backups & recovery
skills.note: Offsite rotation with restores actually tested, not just configured.

skills.name: Migrations
skills.note: Staged host and version moves with rollback points at every step.

skills.name: Monitoring & alerting
skills.note: Uptime, TPS and crash alerts routed to the person who can act on them.

toolbox.title: What I work with daily.
toolbox.kicker: Not an exhaustive list — just the tools I reach for without thinking.

approach.title: Four steps, every time.
approach.kicker: Same process whether it is a single plugin fix or a full network rebuild.

steps.title: Audit
steps.body: I go through what you already have — configs, plugins, roles, staff structure — and write down what is actually broken versus what merely looks messy.

steps.title: Blueprint
steps.body: You get a written plan before I touch anything: what changes, what stays, what it costs in time, and what could go wrong.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Configuration happens on a staging copy wherever possible, with checkpoints so you see progress rather than waiting for a reveal.

steps.title: Handover
steps.body: Written documentation, a walkthrough call, and two weeks of follow-up support. The goal is that you never need to call me again.
